policy_title: Address NHS doctor and nurse shortages
stated: Reform UK will tackle NHS and social care staffing shortages by making all frontline staff pay zero basic rate tax for three years, ending training caps for UK medical students, and writing off student fees pro rata over 10 years of NHS service.

source.quote: End Doctor and Nurse Shortages All frontline NHS and social care staff to pay zero basic rate tax for 3 years. This will help retain existing staff and attract many who have left to return. End training caps for all UK medical students. Write off student fees pro rata per year over 10 years of NHS service for all doctors, nurses and medical staff.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets NHS and social care staffing shortages through tax incentives, training-cap removal, and fee write-offs — all aimed at increasing frontline workforce supply and retention, which drives waiting times and access to care.

Zero basic rate tax for three years is a material take-home pay improvement for a large frontline workforce; independently it affects real wages and job quality for these workers regardless of whether the retention goal is met.

The policy explicitly covers social care staffing, and improved social care staffing levels would directly move the social care access, cost, and waiting-time indicators that define security in later life.

Zero basic rate income tax for all frontline NHS and social care staff for three years is a direct, material improvement to take-home pay for a large workforce, earning a real verdict on household tax burden and distributional incidence.

Exempting hundreds of thousands of frontline NHS/social care workers from basic rate tax for three years, plus pro-rata student loan write-offs, represents substantial foregone revenue; the fiscal cost is large enough to materially affect the funded/borrowed balance and earns a real verdict on public finance sustainability.

membership_note: The three components map cleanly onto O3 (the healthcare staffing objective), O11 (the direct tax relief to workers), and O12 (the significant fiscal cost). Other fundamentals such as O4 (the pay effect is captured under O11), O7 (training cap removal is instrumental to O3, not a general education intervention), and O14 (targeted at a specific workforce rather than the broad income distribution) do not clear the non-negligible bar independently.
